adjudicated 2026-10-03 from source PatchClientValidationTest.java:99-103 at keycloak @ 421c23f5221d. Enumerating every @Disabled in the pinned file returns three, on lines 101, 107 and 113; line 101 holds the annotation itself, so unlike the JWETest rows this citation is sound. @Disabled("Only for PUT/POST") on validSAMLClientSucceeds() - and the method body is EMPTY. It is a subclass override of a base-class validation test, it overrides @Test as well as the base method, asserts nothing, and never runs. So the PATCH path for SAML-client validation is verified by nothing: the test that would check it is disabled, and the neighbouring validSAMLClientSucceeds overrides at :107 and :113 are disabled for the same stated reason. This is the purest instance of the rule's diagnosis in the corpus - a disabled test with no assertions cannot hide a defect, because it could not have detected one. A stated reason does not rescue it: @Disabled('slow, run manually') and @Ignore('keep for reference') are both already adjudicated TP in this file for the same reason.
